claims.title: Meeting 1A. Quantifiers, proof and numerical evidence
claims.week: Week 1. Logic: why many tests are not a proof
claims.goal: Separate a universal statement from an arbitrarily long finite verification.
claims.body:
Target: Separate a universal statement from an arbitrarily long finite verification.
Entry (10 min): Ask: a program verifies a property for one million inputs. Does it follow that (a) the property holds for the tested inputs, or (b) it holds for all inputs? Only (a) follows without additional proof.
Instruction (20 min): Compare ,  and  for finite . A valid counterexample refutes a universal claim; positive finite observations usually do not establish one.
Worked task (30 min): For each integer , define . Check  for  yet . Thus even a million checks can mislead.
Research transfer (20 min): RH asserts that all nontrivial zeros  of the analytically continued Riemann zeta satisfy . Checking zeros up to a finite height is not the same proposition.

claims.title: Meeting 1B. Design a claim–evidence–gap record
claims.week: Week 1. Logic: why many tests are not a proof
claims.goal: Classify examples, experiments, conditional statements and proofs.
claims.body:
Target: Classify examples, experiments, conditional statements and proofs.
Opening (10 min): Present the screenshot-visible video question: can brute-force AI computation replace mathematical insight? Do not attribute any additional spoken argument to the presenter.
Concept (20 min): Introduce the fields claim, definitions, assumptions, finite evidence, independent check, missing implication and certification status.
Group repair (30 min): Replace “one million zeta functions prove RH” with a bounded description: “Numerical features were evaluated for specified families; this provides no theorem relating every genuine Riemann zero to the critical line.”
Adversarial review (20 min): Find an assumption hidden by feature normalization; propose a control that might create a false loop.

claims.title: Meeting 4B. Three spaces, three topological questions
claims.goal: Separate topology of the graph, the associated function and an observed descriptor cloud.
claims.body:
Target: Separate topology of the graph, the associated function and an observed descriptor cloud.
The connected cycle graph  has ,  and graph Betti number .
The Ihara zeta is a rational function , with its own analytic and algebraic data.
The measured cloud  lives in a selected metric feature space. Under the adaptive probes from 4A, it collapses to one unique point, so its one-dimensional homology is zero.
There is no contradiction between the cycle graph having a loop and its measurement cloud having none: they are different topological objects.

claims.title: Meeting 6A. Pre-register and stress-test a bounded experiment
claims.week: Week 6. From a computational pattern to a defensible claim
claims.goal: Record every choice that determines what the reported result means.
claims.body:
Target: Record every choice that determines what the reported result means.
Students choose one of three small experiments: spectral values for ; fixed versus adaptive Ihara measurements; or the square’s VR filtration. Before testing, they write down the object, input range, metric/feature map, computational precision, expected positive and negative controls, and a possible countercheck. An exact algebraic derivation is required even for coding submissions.
10 min: Quiz on universal quantifiers and evidence.
20 min: Select and pre-register the experiment.
30 min: Carry it out with code or exact hand calculations.

claims.title: Claim audit: finite checks do not establish RH
claims.goal: Evaluate the missing inference from computational zeta/TDA observations to universal Riemann-zero statements
claims.body: The curriculum distinguishes finite numerical experiments on selected zeta-function descriptors from a proof that every actual nontrivial zero of analytically continued Riemann zeta lies on the critical line. A valid bridge theorem is not supplied.
claims.source_section: Curriculum at a glance; Week 1; Appendix B

claims.title: Exact counterexample: adaptive Ihara measurements alias
claims.goal: Review the exact n-independent adaptive probe and its measurement limitation
claims.body: For the cycle Ihara zeta Z_n(u)=(1-u^n)^(-2), the adaptive probe u_n=exp(-t/n) yields Z_n(u_n)=(1-exp(-t))^(-2), independent of n. The measured descriptor can collapse even though the underlying rational functions differ.
